title: Retorsion: tradition is as silent as Scripture on when Antichrist comes
source_text: XIX. Sed, quod maxime notandum est, rogo Pontificios annon ex Scriptura & traditione simul integra Apostoli doctrina haberi possit? Proculdubio istud non negabunt. Doceant ergo nos ex traditione quando dixit Apostolus Thessalonicensibus venturum esse Antichristum. Certe hic non minus tacet traditio, quam Scriptura sacra. Itaque, si quis est hac in re defectus, ejus non minus traditio, quam Scriptura sacra incusari potest. Si vero hoc non obstat quominus tota Apostoli doctrina possit haberi ex traditione, non obstabit etiam quo minus possit haberi ex Scriptura.
pass_a_gloss: But what is most to be noted, I ask the Pontificians whether the entire doctrine of the Apostle cannot be had from Scripture and tradition together? Doubtless they will not deny that. Let them therefore teach us from tradition when the Apostle told the Thessalonians that the Antichrist was to come. Certainly here tradition is no less silent than sacred Scripture. Therefore, if there is any defect in this matter, tradition no less than sacred Scripture can be blamed for it. But if this does not hinder that the whole doctrine of the Apostle can be had from tradition, it will also not hinder that it can be had from Scripture.
pass_b_english: Ask them: can the whole apostolic doctrine be had from Scripture and tradition together? They will say yes.
Then teach from tradition the Antichrist timetable Paul allegedly gave.
Tradition is as mute as Scripture here.
If that silence does not wreck their tradition-rule, it does not wreck sola Scriptura either.
